out_of_taxonomy.concept: industry domains other than finance/payments and healthcare (e-commerce/marketplace economics, supply chain/manufacturing, HR/people analytics, games, ads, robotics/autonomy)
out_of_taxonomy.reason: each recurs in only 1-3 JDs per sample and mostly reflects the employer, not a transferable skill; finance and healthcare are kept as domain_finance / domain_healthcare because they recur and carry regulated-data skills

out_of_taxonomy.concept: embedded / firmware, hardware enclaves, edge platforms
out_of_taxonomy.reason: seen once each; too rare across the 10 titles to compare prevalence

out_of_taxonomy.concept: enterprise application support (troubleshooting, configuration, implementations), vendor evaluation
out_of_taxonomy.reason: phrasing is too generic for a precise regex; partly covered by erp_systems and system_integration

out_of_taxonomy.concept: generic organisational / teamwork skills, public speaking
out_of_taxonomy.reason: not concrete enough to count reliably; covered in part by stakeholder_communication and project_management

out_of_taxonomy.concept: SDLC (software development lifecycle) as a named skill
out_of_taxonomy.reason: removed in v2026-10-03b: in train and precision JDs it mostly appeared in company or product blurbs ('complete SDLC for millions of developers'), not as an ask; actual practices are covered by ci_cd, testing_qa, code_review, agile_jira
tried in v2026-10-03c; matched 1 of 113 train JDs, below the 2-JD floor; workshops are partly covered by enablement_training

out_of_taxonomy.concept: dataset creation / versioned datasets, human-in-the-loop infrastructure
out_of_taxonomy.reason: single mentions in the gate-2 holdout; not recurring in train
dropped in v2026-10-03: in train JDs the words mostly appeared in company blurbs ('innovative algorithms'), 3 JDs after fixing
